content:
SAMUEL ACHTERBERG-OSEI
Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Engineer

[EMAIL] | [PHONE] | [LINKEDIN]

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Cloud infrastructure engineer with experience designing, building and operating Azure environments, infrastructure as code and deployment pipelines. Currently delivering Azure landing-zone networking, Terraform modules and CI/CD pipelines for internal applications. Previously supported approximately 250 Windows and Linux servers and led a 60-server VMware-to-Azure migration completed over six weekends without unplanned downtime. Practical experience with Azure networking, AKS operations, PowerShell automation and Microsoft 365 security baselines.

CORE SKILLS
Cloud and infrastructure: Microsoft Azure, Azure IaaS, Azure landing zones, Azure VMs, Azure Migrate, App Service, AKS operations
Infrastructure as code and automation: Terraform, Terraform modules, PowerShell, drift detection
Networking: Hub-and-spoke networks, VNets, VNet peering, Azure Firewall, private DNS zones, private endpoints, site-to-site VPN
DevOps and containers: Azure DevOps YAML pipelines, Docker, Helm, CI/CD, Terratest (Go)
Systems and security: Windows and Linux servers, VMware, Microsoft 365, Entra ID, MFA, Conditional Access, mailbox auditing, backups
Scripting: PowerShell; Python for reading and writing small scripts

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Cloud Engineer (Contract) | Havenstad Logistics | 2025–Present
- Build and maintain Azure landing-zone networking using Terraform, including hub-and-spoke architecture, Azure Firewall, private DNS zones, private endpoints for storage and SQL, and VNet peering across three subscriptions.
- Add Terratest module tests to Azure DevOps pipelines and implement a nightly infrastructure drift-detection job.
- Replaced manual deployments for 15 internal .NET and Node applications with Azure DevOps YAML pipelines for build, test and deployment to App Service or AKS.
- Increased deployment frequency from roughly monthly to several times per week for most applications.
- Operate AKS, including upgrades, node pools and ingress; application manifests are owned by development teams.

Freelance IT Support | 2022–2023
- Created a repeatable PowerShell script and checklist for small-business Microsoft 365 security baselines.
- Enabled MFA, Conditional Access, mailbox auditing and backups for small clients.

Systems Administrator | Maasbrug Gemeente IT Services | 2014–March 2020
- Administered Windows and Linux systems and supported staff across several municipal services.
- Looked after approximately 250 Windows and Linux servers.
- Led the 2019 migration of 60 servers from VMware to Azure IaaS using Azure Migrate; completed cutover over six weekends with no unplanned downtime.
- Used PowerShell to automate repetitive work.

CAREER BREAKS AND PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT

March 2020–August 2022 | Family caregiving
- Left municipal employment to provide full-time care for a family member.
- Kept Azure Administrator Associate knowledge current and provided unpaid IT help to church and family.

February 2024–February 2025 | Professional development
- Completed a part-time, online, English-language cloud bootcamp in December 2024.
- Studied Terraform and passed the Terraform Associate certification in 2025.
- Built a Proxmox homelab.

CERTIFICATIONS
- Microsoft Certified: Azure Administrator Associate (AZ-104)
- Terraform Associate (2025)

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION
- Dutch driving licence

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is well structured, concise, professional and easy to scan. It presents strong quantified evidence: approximately 250 servers, a 60-server migration, 15 application pipelines, three Azure subscriptions and improved deployment frequency. The progression from systems administration to cloud engineering is credible, and the career breaks are explained transparently. The strongest content is the Azure infrastructure, Terraform, networking, migration and automation experience. The main content limitation is that several bullets describe implementation but do not explicitly show systems-design reasoning, stakeholder engagement or technical proposal leadership, which are important for this role. The contact details are also still placeholders, making the document incomplete for submission.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The section headings, reverse-chronological experience and standard text formatting are ATS-friendly. The CV contains highly relevant searchable terms including Azure, Terraform, Azure landing zones, Azure DevOps, AKS, Docker, Helm, Azure Firewall, private endpoints, VNets, PowerShell, Linux, VMware and Azure Migrate. AI screening probability is good to high for Azure-focused infrastructure roles, but moderate for this specific vacancy because the CV does not contain Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, AWS, IoT or explicit stakeholder/system-design terminology. These are genuine experience gaps or unsupported requirements, so they should not be added without evidence. The placeholder contact fields may also prevent reliable parsing or make the application appear unfinished.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV is a strong match for hands-on cloud infrastructure engineering, Azure environment design and operation, Terraform, networking, practical security, Linux, virtual machines and operational reliability. The Azure landing-zone project and VMware-to-Azure migration are particularly relevant to designing and operating production infrastructure. The candidate also demonstrates technical ownership through leading the 60-server migration and replacing manual deployments with pipelines. Important gaps for this role are Terragrunt, mTLS/certificate management, SSL/TLS experience, AWS, IoT or remote-device integration, and a JVM/backend development background. The CV also provides limited direct evidence of agreeing interfaces with external stakeholders or leading technical proposals across backend and infrastructure. These are job-alignment gaps rather than defects that can be solved by rewriting. The document does not currently establish experience with train, automotive or fleet connectivity systems.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL: In the contact-information line beneath the name and title, replace "[EMAIL] | [PHONE] | [LINKEDIN]" with the candidate’s actual professional email address, phone number and LinkedIn URL. Remove the square-bracket placeholders before submitting.

MINOR: In the Professional Summary, make the existing technical leadership and system-design evidence more explicit without adding unsupported claims. For example, revise the opening to: "Cloud infrastructure engineer with experience designing, building and operating Azure environments, infrastructure as code and deployment pipelines. Currently delivering Azure landing-zone networking, Terraform modules and CI/CD pipelines for internal applications, with ownership of infrastructure design, testing and operational reliability." Only use this wording if it accurately reflects the candidate’s responsibilities.

MINOR: In the Cloud Engineer experience section, revise the first bullet so that the architecture scope is clearer and uses the job ad’s terminology where supported. For example: "Design and maintain Azure landing-zone networking using Terraform, including hub-and-spoke architecture, Azure Firewall, private DNS zones, private endpoints for storage and SQL, and VNet peering across three subscriptions." Do not add Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS or certificate management because the original candidate information does not support them.

MINOR: In the Systems Administrator experience section, strengthen the existing technical-leadership evidence by changing "Led the 2019 migration of 60 servers from VMware to Azure IaaS using Azure Migrate" to "Led the planning and execution of the 2019 migration of 60 servers from VMware to Azure IaaS using Azure Migrate; completed the cutover over six weekends with no unplanned downtime." This is supported by the candidate’s portfolio and more clearly demonstrates ownership and delivery.
critique.critical_issues: The CV contains unfinished contact placeholders: "[EMAIL] | [PHONE] | [LINKEDIN]". These must be replaced with actual contact details before submission. No unsupported skills, tools, certifications or experiences were detected when cross-referenced against the Original Candidate Information.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a clear, well-structured and professional CV with a strong cloud infrastructure focus. The summary quickly establishes Azure, Terraform, CI/CD, networking and operational experience. The experience section contains credible scope and outcomes, including 250 servers, a 60-server migration with no unplanned downtime, 15 application pipelines and increased deployment frequency. Career breaks are explained transparently and professionally. The main content limitation is that some role-relevant areas—technical stakeholder leadership, system design, certificate-based security and analytical decision-making—are not evidenced, although the supplied candidate information also does not provide substantive evidence for several of them.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The document is highly ATS-compatible: it uses standard section headings, conventional reverse-chronological structure, readable text formatting and strong Azure, Terraform, networking, CI/CD, Linux, VMware and security keywords. It should parse well and has a strong AI-screening probability for Azure-focused infrastructure roles. Alignment would improve if the experience bullets explicitly included the supported migration networking technologies (VNets and site-to-site VPN) rather than leaving them only in the skills section. Terragrunt, mTLS and SSL/TLS are absent, but these are candidate capability gaps rather than keywords that should be added without evidence.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV strongly demonstrates hands-on infrastructure engineering and Azure cloud environment design and operation. It also shows practical Terraform, networking, security awareness, Linux and virtual-machine experience. Azure is an acceptable major-cloud background because the advertisement states that AWS is preferred but other major clouds are acceptable. The candidate's material does not show Terragrunt, AWS, mTLS, SSL/TLS, IoT or automotive/remote-device integration, or JVM/full-stack development; these are gaps rather than document defects. The document shows some relevant leadership through leading the 60-server migration, but it does not establish experience bringing external stakeholders or technical stakeholders along. The current evidence also does not explicitly demonstrate system-design decision-making, observability, or clear analytical/communication outcomes in the terms used by the advertisement. No specific company-culture claims should be added because the candidate information does not document them.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR, ATS/alignment enhancement:
1. In the Systems Administrator experience section, revise the Azure migration bullet to include the supported networking scope from the candidate portfolio. For example, change it to: "Led the planning and execution of the 2019 migration of 60 servers from VMware to Azure IaaS using Azure Migrate, Azure VMs, VNets and site-to-site VPN; completed the cutover over six weekends with no unplanned downtime." This brings relevant networking keywords into the experience section, where ATS and recruiters give them more weight.

2. In the Professional Summary, replace the broad phrase "ownership of infrastructure design, testing and operational reliability" with more concrete evidence already documented. For example: "...with responsibility for Azure landing-zone network design, Terraform module testing, drift detection and operational reliability." This is more specific and better reflects the documented Havenstad work.

3. In the Cloud Engineer experience section, make the technical scope of the AKS work slightly more explicit without implying application-manifest ownership. Change the final bullet to: "Operate AKS clusters, including upgrades, node-pool management and ingress configuration; development teams own the application manifests." This preserves the important boundary already stated in the CV while making the infrastructure responsibility clearer.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured CV with a clear cloud infrastructure and Azure DevOps focus. The Professional Summary is targeted, the experience bullets are specific, and several achievements include credible scale or outcome measures, particularly the 250-server estate, 60-server migration, 15 application pipelines, and increase in deployment frequency. The document is professional and easy to scan. Career breaks are disclosed transparently and explained appropriately. The main content limitation is that some role-relevant capabilities are implied rather than stated explicitly, especially systems architecture/system design, technical leadership, stakeholder engagement, and clear communication. The CV also does not distinguish sufficiently between demonstrated requirements and areas outside the candidate's stated experience.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses conventional section headings, standard reverse-chronological experience, simple text formatting, and strong searchable keywords including Azure, Terraform, Azure DevOps, CI/CD, AKS, networking, PowerShell, Linux, VMware, security, and virtual machines. It should parse well in most ATS systems, with a good AI-screening probability for Azure-focused infrastructure roles. Keyword coverage is weaker for this specific vacancy because Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, certificate management, systems architecture, system design, stakeholder engagement, and observability are not clearly represented. These are genuine experience gaps or unsupported areas rather than terms that should be added without evidence. The phrase "Python for reading and writing small scripts" is truthful but appropriately qualified.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns strongly with the hands-on infrastructure engineering, cloud environment design and operation, Terraform, networking, practical security, Linux, and virtual-machine aspects of the role. Azure is an acceptable major-cloud background even though AWS is preferred. The landing-zone architecture, Terraform module testing, drift detection, Azure DevOps pipelines, AKS operations, and VMware-to-Azure migration are relevant to a platform that must be reliable and secure. The candidate also demonstrates technical ownership through leading the 60-server migration and delivering infrastructure changes. However, the candidate material does not show Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, certificate management, IoT or remote-device integration, JVM/backend development, or direct experience agreeing interfaces with external manufacturers. Stakeholder leadership and formal system-design ownership are only partially evidenced. These are job-alignment gaps, not document defects, and should not be implied as existing experience.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR, HIGH-VALUE IMPROVEMENTS:
1. In the Professional Summary, replace the final sentence with wording that makes supported architecture and ownership more explicit: "Practical experience with Azure networking, systems infrastructure, AKS operations, PowerShell automation and Microsoft 365 security baselines, including leading a 60-server VMware-to-Azure migration with no unplanned downtime." This avoids overstating unsupported mTLS, Terragrunt or AWS experience while strengthening the system-design signal.
2. In the Cloud Engineer experience section, revise the first bullet to begin with the supported design responsibility: "Design and maintain Azure landing-zone network architecture in Terraform, including..." Keep the existing technical details. This better matches the advertisement's cloud environment design and systems architecture language.
3. In the Cloud Engineer experience section, revise the pipeline bullet to make the technical leadership and developer collaboration that are actually evidenced more visible: "Replaced manual deployments for 15 internal .NET and Node applications by designing and implementing Azure DevOps YAML pipelines for build, test and deployment to App Service or AKS, supporting development teams with repeatable release processes." Do not claim formal stakeholder management or ownership of application manifests.
4. In the Systems Administrator experience section, revise "Led the planning and execution of the 2019 migration..." to "Led the technical planning and execution of the 2019 migration..." because the candidate's material supports leadership of this technical topic. Retain the six-weekend cutover and no-unplanned-downtime result.
5. In the Core Skills section, change the heading "DevOps and containers" to "DevOps, CI/CD and containers" and retain the existing terms. This gives the ATS a closer match to the job's deployment and platform language without adding unsupported tools.
6. In the Career Breaks and Professional Development section, clarify the chronology around the overlapping 2022 dates. For example, change the freelance heading to "Freelance IT Support | 2022–2023" and add a short parenthetical in the caregiving entry such as "Family caregiving continued until August 2022; freelance support work began during 2022." Use this only if it accurately reflects the actual timing.
7. In the Core Skills section, retain "Linux and virtual machines" as searchable wording, for example: "Systems and security: Windows and Linux servers, VMware virtual machines, Microsoft 365..." This uses the advertisement's terminology while remaining fully supported.
